findings.title: Master-data opening balance uses a JSON string where SQL requires a JSON number
findings.root_cause: createOpening assigns poundsToPiastres' string directly to signed_piastres; JSON.stringify therefore emits a string. app_exact_bigint explicitly rejects JSON values whose jsonb_typeof is not number.
findings.reproduction: Using isolated fixtures, submit a valid Master Data contractor or vehicle-cash opening. Its wire payload contains signed_piastres: "100". The DB validation rejects SQLSTATE 22023 and the intended opening is not recorded.
findings.expected: A valid, exactly-representable opening is saved atomically, while inputs outside safe-auth JSON/bigint bounds fail explicitly before mutation.
findings.actual: Both opening types in this existing UI path fail at DB numeric validation instead of saving.
findings.impact: A user cannot enter old opening balances through the visible Master Data workflow. This is a financial write-path availability failure; no existing production row was changed or proven duplicated during this review.
findings.evidence: Complete UI string conversion to JSON/HTTP to app_exact_bigint source trace on main. Historical docs/ISSUES.md:217-218 independently identifies the same separate unresolved path; final fixture output is being recorded separately.
findings.recommended_action: Use a tested exact opening serializer at this UI boundary: convert only after BigInt validation and only if the exact signed integer is safely representable in this JSON/API contract, otherwise refuse explicitly. Add actual isolated SQL tests for both types, signs, rounding, safe-integer boundary and replay.
findings.fix_regression_risk: HIGH: naive Number conversion loses financial precision; tests must cover negatives, bigint bounds, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and old quick openings, and must preserve idempotency payload identity.

findings.title: PR #98 misses revision-driven contractor loading and error reset
findings.root_cause: Revision invalidation duplicates part of reset rather than calling it. On PR #98, reset clears busy and error, but the revision effect only increments active/query=null/report=null. If a prior request is delayed or invalidated, the new revision can retain its prior busy/error state independent of correct latest-response guards.
findings.reproduction: Start/delay a contractor initial or more request; change revision while awaiting; inspect the disabled/loading and stale alert state before/while the old promise resolves. Run same test with repeated rapid revisions and unmounting.
findings.expected: Every invalidated report generation becomes editable/retryable and cannot retain or reinstate an obsolete alert/loading state.
findings.actual: On PR #98 the revision-only path does not clear busy or error. Existing disabled fields can therefore be left waiting on the invalid request's own lifecycle.
findings.impact: The contractor statement can lock loading/actions or display stale errors after writes/refresh invalidation. Stored financial rows are not shown to be affected.
findings.evidence: Comparison of PR #98 head b0b3bde7 with main; separate effect uses setReport only, while fixed reset() includes busy clearing; token-only finally guards prevent old cleanup from repairing that new revision state.
findings.recommended_action: Route all invalidation causes through one reset protocol including busy/error cleanup and request-generation guards. Add deterministic deferred-response component tests for revision changes during first and later page reads and old errors.
findings.fix_regression_risk: MEDIUM: cleanup must not enable a premature duplicate fetch or let older completion update current rows; preserve token checks on every asynchronous write/finally.

findings.title: Portable backup is assembled from separate offset-based requests without snapshot consistency
findings.confidence: Confirmed (structural absence); Needs verification for live incidence
findings.root_cause: The GET route separately reads each table via offset pagination. No repeatable-read database transaction spans those HTTP requests, no global ledger snapshot/revision is checked, and createPortableBackup verifies presence/types/sha256 but not cross-request consistency.
findings.reproduction: Use only a synthetic isolated database and mocked multi-page PostgREST responses. Commit a synthetic edit/cancellation between page calls or a related-entity update between two table reads; prove exported rows cannot be assigned to one MVCC snapshot while the returned backup still succeeds.
findings.expected: A backup is one complete point-in-time snapshot, or fails explicitly on revision drift.
findings.actual: Each page/table can see a different committed state and the result is serialized as a coherent archival backup with creation timestamp and checksum but no snapshot validation.
findings.impact: In an active ledger, a portable recovery export can silently combine different versions of related financial records. This is a recovery-integrity risk. It says nothing defective about the separately reviewed offsite MVCC/pg_dump pipeline.
findings.evidence: Source shows repeated await client.from(table).range(...) requests with no snapshot parameter, read transaction, revision guard, or final comparison. backup row_counts and SHA-256 describe bytes, not atomic isolation.
findings.recommended_action: Implement/reuse a database snapshot/revision export protocol that covers all target tables and fails closed on any concurrent drift. Add isolated multi-page concurrency, FK-related update, replay and full recovery-fingerprint verification.
findings.fix_regression_risk: HIGH: backup schema/adapters/gates and restoration tooling must remain compatible; a superficial revision count on audit_log may not cover all tables and can produce false completeness. Do not modify production while addressing this finding.

findings.title: Playwright browser acceptance is blocked by missing Chromium
findings.root_cause: The required Playwright Chromium executable is not installed in the audit environment.
findings.reproduction: Run npm run test:workspace without the pinned browser installed.
findings.actual: Browser launch fails before application assertions.
findings.recommended_action: Install the pinned browser in CI and rerun the complete workspace suite.
